subject: Draft concept: produce codes for new cashiers
mail: Here's my concept card for the supermarket. New cashiers make too many errors keying in fruit and vegetable codes in their first weeks. Can you give it a last look?
snippets: About 300 produce codes exist; 40 cover 85% of sales.
Errors are highest in a cashier's first two weeks.
Each store has one training till that's rarely used.
draft: Big idea: new cashiers learn the 40 most-sold produce codes by heart, not all 300.
Format: two 10-minute practice rounds on the training till in the first week, plus a code card at every till.
An experienced buddy cashier stands nearby for the first three shifts.
What it is NOT: a classroom course on all store procedures.
Success is measured by the number of new cashiers who complete both practice rounds.
Risk: weekend rush leaves no time for practice; mitigation: schedule practice rounds on Tuesday mornings.
flaw_why: Completing the practice rounds says nothing about errors at the till, which is the problem the concept is meant to fix.
fix: Measure produce code errors per cashier in their first two weeks from the till data, compared with new cashiers before the change.
debrief: The concept is sharp and well scoped; only its success measure slipped into counting attendance. Till systems log corrections and voids, so the real result is available for free.
